title: Addressable transversal T gates on good quantum LDPC codes
source: Lin, Wu and Cheng pose this question in Section~6, item~2, with a fixed encoding and bounded weight and participation. Meiburg asks for the same combination of addressability, sparsity, rate and distance in Section~6 \sourcecite{ref:atq-lwc}{LWC26}, \sourcecite{ref:atq-meiburg}{Mei26}.
progress: Lin, Wu and Cheng, Theorem~4.5, construct asymptotically good binary CSS codes with fully addressable logical $T$ implemented by physical powers of $T$. The construction has no uniformly bounded check-weight and participation guarantee \sourcecite{ref:atq-lwc}{LWC26}. Wu, Lin, and Cheng improve the guaranteed rate and relative distance in Theorems~1 and~2. Uniform sparsity of Pauli checks remains open for these constructions \sourcecite{ref:atq-wlc}{WLC26}.

Meiburg, Sections~4--5, obtains sparse Pauli checks with transversal $T$ at vanishing rate and a separate protected-subsystem construction with constant protected rate, distance $\Omega(\sqrt n)$, and sparse, generally non-Pauli checks \sourcecite{ref:atq-meiburg}{Mei26}.

Li, Li, Han and Liu, Theorem~1.1 and Section~3.4, construct good binary quantum LDPC codes with addressable transversal logical controlled-phase gates across code blocks \sourcecite{ref:atq-llhl}{LLHL26}. Under a product-expansion hypothesis, Tan and Zhu obtain individually addressable logical CCZ gates on disjoint triples, with distance $\Omega_\epsilon(n/\log^2 n)$ in Theorem~1.2 \sourcecite{ref:atq-tz}{TZ26}.

comment: The target is a diagonal one-qubit action on a chosen logical index of one block. The related \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_15c6d5adf1796d86/}{transversal CCZ question} uses three blocks, and the \href{https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_ddfbbe7ca0ead0c8/}{six-qubit transversal $T$ question} concerns one fixed code size. The catalog and literature were checked through November 26, 2026.
